## Counting using summarise

You might be familiar with 

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data |> 
  dplyr::summarise(count_types = dplyr::n(), .by = type)

```

:::{.callout-tip collapse=false appearance='default' icon=true}
This uses the `.by()` argument is is _temporary grouping_ and is dropped after running the code. 

Using `group_by()` is [persistent grouping](https://intro-r-rstudio.nhsrcommunity.com/session-dplyr-wrangling.html#/group_by---temporary-grouping).
:::


## A specific function to count

Simply use a function called count to count:

```{r}
data |> 
  dplyr::count(type)
```

This is similar to `summarise()` which condenses the data frame to the count columns.

## Adding a total column

But you might be familiar with `mutate()` and want to adds the column to the data frame:

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::mutate(count = dplyr::n(), .by = type)
```

## Quicker way to add total column

The column name defaults to n for `number`

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::add_count(type)

```

The function has additional arguments like name and sort

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::add_count(type, 
                   name = "total_type",
                   sort = TRUE)
```
